verifications.claim: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends visiting a travel medicine specialist or your healthcare provider 4–6 weeks before departure to discuss your itinerary and receive tailored advice.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Make an appointment with your healthcare provider or a travel health specialist that takes place at least 4-6 weeks before you leave. They can help you get destination-specific vaccines, medicines, and information. Discussing your health concerns, itinerary, and planned activities with your provider allows them to give more specific advice and recommendations.' R8: 'Talk with a trusted healthcare professional or a travel health specialist at least 4-6 weeks before you travel'
verifications.reasoning: Direct match in multiple sources specifying 4-6 weeks and discussion of itinerary for tailored advice.

verifications.claim: Specific countries in Africa and South America require proof of yellow fever vaccination (Yellow Card).

verifications.evidence: R3: 'When proof of vaccination against YF is required by a country on the traveler's itinerary' R6: 'Some countries require, proof of yellow fever vaccination... International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP)' R11: 'Some countries in South America and Africa require you to provide proof... International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis'

verifications.claim: The Yellow Card is only valid 10 days after administration.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Documentation of vaccination against YF on the International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP) becomes valid 10 days after administration.' R6: 'Your proof of vaccination is not valid until 10 days after you get the vaccine' R11: 'the proof of vaccination does not become valid until 10 days after the vaccine is given.'
verifications.reasoning: Exact match for ICVP/Yellow Card validity starting 10 days post-administration.

verifications.claim: Yellow fever vaccination is required for entry into certain countries in Africa and South America.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'If yellow fever vaccine is recommended or required for your destination' R3: 'proof of vaccination against YF is required by a country' R6: 'Some countries require... yellow fever vaccination before entering the country' R11: 'Some countries in South America and Africa require... yellow fever'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources specify requirements for entry in Africa and South America.

verifications.claim: Hepatitis A vaccination is recommended for most travelers going to countries with poor food/water sanitation.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: lists 'Hepatitis A' as possible vaccine for travel R7: 'Vaccination is recommended for all children traveling to areas with an intermediate or high risk for hepatitis A' R14: lists Hepatitis A as routine for travel R15: 'Recommended for unvaccinated travelers... going to Brazil'
verifications.reasoning: Standard recommendation tied to poor sanitation areas; directly supported though phrasing is general.

verifications.claim: Typhoid vaccination is recommended for travelers visiting South Asia (India, Pakistan, Bangladesh) or other areas with high risk.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: lists 'Typhoid' as possible vaccine R4: lists 'Typhoid Fever' R5: 'XDR Typhoid Fever in Pakistan' R15: 'Recommended for most travelers... Typhoid'
verifications.reasoning: Recommended for high-risk areas including South Asia (e.g., Pakistan specific), but not exclusively listing India/Pakistan/Bangladesh.

verifications.claim: Japanese Encephalitis vaccination is recommended for long-term travel (≥1 month) or rural visits in Asia.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R7: 'JE vaccine is recommended for travelers who plan to spend ≥1 month (consecutive or cumulative) in endemic areas during JE virus transmission season and can be considered for short-term (<1 month) travelers whose itinerary or activities could increase their risk... Asia'
verifications.reasoning: Precise match for ≥1 month in Asia and higher risk for rural activities.

verifications.claim: Meningococcal Disease vaccination is recommended for the African meningitis belt.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R7: 'Children aged 2 months to 18 years who travel to or reside in areas of Sub-Saharan Africa known as the meningitis belt during the dry season (December–June) should receive quadrivalent meningococcal conjugate (MenACWY) vaccine.'
verifications.reasoning: Direct recommendation for African meningitis belt.

verifications.claim: Meningococcal Disease vaccination is required for Hajj/Umrah travelers to Saudi Arabia.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Meningococcal Quadrivalent (ACWY) meningococcal vaccine is required for all individuals 1 year of age and older traveling to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia for religious pilgrimages. Hajj visas will not be issued without proof' R7: 'Travelers are required to have meningococcal vaccination to enter Saudi Arabia when traveling to Mecca for Umrah or the annual Hajj pilgrimage.'
verifications.reasoning: Explicit requirement for Hajj/Umrah to Saudi Arabia.

verifications.claim: Rabies vaccination is recommended for travelers visiting areas where dog bites are common or for long-stay or rural travelers.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: lists 'Rabies' R3: 'rabies pre-exposure vaccination... sustained risk for rabies exposure' R7: 'pre-exposure... for children... mainly from dogs... low- and middle-income countries' R15: 'Dogs infected with rabies are sometimes found... pre-exposure vaccination considerations'
verifications.reasoning: Recommended for high-risk areas with dog bites, long-stay, rural travel.

verifications.claim: Tick-borne Encephalitis (TBE) vaccination is recommended for travelers going to TBE-endemic areas in Europe or Asia who plan outdoor activities.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: lists 'Tick-borne encephalitis' R3: 'For LMTs traveling to a TBE-endemic area' R7: 'recommended for use among people traveling... to a TBE-endemic area who will have extensive tick exposure based on planned outdoor activities... parts of Asia and Europe'
verifications.reasoning: Direct recommendation for TBE-endemic Europe/Asia with outdoor activities.

verifications.claim: The minimum time needed for yellow fever vaccine to become effective for entry requirements is 10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Travelers who receive YF vaccine <10 days before entering a risk area are at risk... becomes valid 10 days after administration.' R6: 'not valid until 10 days after you get the vaccine because of the time it takes for your body to build protection.'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm 10 days minimum for effectiveness and entry validity.

verifications.claim: Hepatitis A vaccine can still offer protection if given less than 2 weeks before travel.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Hepatitis A (monovalent)... single-dose protection Even with limited time before departure' R7: 'Ideally... ≥2 weeks before travel but providing a dose as late as the day of travel is acceptable.' R9: 'some multiple-dose vaccines (like hepatitis A) can still give you partial protection after just one dose.'
verifications.reasoning: Sources state single dose provides some/protection even close to or on day of travel.
